pro-inflammatory cytokines are predictive of relapse-free survival in intermediate risk melanoma patients treated with aduivant IFN-α.
the cytokine profiles of melanoma patients are differentially altered by adjuvant therapy and that these differences may be used as a biomarker to predict response to treatment.
proinflammatory cytokines are associated with RFS in patients receiving adjuvant IFNa-2b, and this association is independent from the HLA genotype and the CTLA-4 and FOXP-3 polymorphisms.

the marker profile is different between Arm A (observation) and Arm B (IFN-α2B) patients.
